content:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV-2 — APAC (azure-southeastasia) Private deployments losing egress to on-prem via VPN and ExpressRoute. Multiple customer reports.
avery: oncall here, paging in. Seeing alerts for 3 private clusters in ap-southeast asia with failed healthchecks and BGP disconnects.
chen: I see BGP withdraws from the virtualWAN hub in SEA-1, timestamps around 02:12Z. Route table looks like routes to customer prefixes removed.
lena: tagging the customers impacted: cust-alpha, cust-greystone, and a private testbed we use for CI. Any packet drops shown?
john: from our side logs show TCP handshakes to customer VPN gateways failing with RST from our egress NAT. Nothing on app level yet.
kate: I already opened CS tickets for cust-alpha and cust-greystone. They report timeouts for admin consoles and marketplace webhooks. Customers are asking if this is an internal issue.
avery: Okay, quick triage: is it just SEA region or cross-region? Can we fail traffic to APAC-secondary (azure-eastasia)?
chen: Preliminary: the virtualWAN hub's route table had a partial corruption after a Microsoft control-plane redeploy. Some prefixes lost next-hops to our ExpressRoute circuits. Azure portal shows "Hub route table: inconsistent".
azure-support: Microsoft support case #232145 opened. We are investigating a controller-side snapshot rollback that coincided with a maintenance window.
ops-oncall: @avery please run the healthcheck/failover playbook. Need to know if we can trigger our traffic-shift to eastasia without customer config changes.
avery: Running playbook now. Steps: 1) verify route-table snapshot 2) reprogram local route cache 3) failover BGP sessions to backup peering 4) communicate to customers.
(avery posts): ```sh
# check route table
az network vwan hub route-table list --resource-group r-infra --hub-name vwan-sea
```
chen: I'll try a manual route import from our known-good snapshot. If Azure control-plane refuses, we need to create static routes in the hub as temporary measure.
john: Note: if we create static routes we'll need to flush KV caches and restart the egress proxies for those clusters, brief 5-10s hiccup expected.
kate: Customers want an ETA. Can we give 30-60 minutes?
avery: Tentative ETA 45m if manual static routes accepted. If we need provider intervention could be longer.
chen: Update: Azure control-plane is rate-limiting our route patch requests. Support is escalating to engineering. They've acknowledged a bug in vWAN route-table replication.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20270315-SEA-VWAN-ROUTE. Severity set to SEV-2. Runbook: APAC-vwan-route-corruption.
lena: Please capture exact customer impact matrix. John/Chen, ping me when you have the list of prefixes missing.
chen: Missing prefixes: 203.0.113.0/24 (cust-alpha), 198.51.100.0/24 (cust-greystone), 198.51.101.0/24 (ci-private).
ajohn: Confirmed those three. Application metrics show increased 502s for cust-alpha's webhook endpoints starting 02:13Z.
avery: Executed manual static route injection on vwan hub for the three prefixes to point at backup ExpressRoute circuit. Azure accepted for now.
(avery posts): ```sh
az network vwan hub route add --hub-name vwan-sea --name temp-cust-alpha --address-prefix 203.0.113.0/24 --next-hop-type VirtualNetworkGateway
```
chen: BGP sessions re-established after static route; monitoring shows prefix glued back and BGP paths restored. Performing connectivity tests to customer gateways.
john: From app telemetry, cust-alpha webhook success rate climbed from 12% to 98% over the last 6 minutes. CI private testbed still showing intermittent DNS timeouts — think that's a separate propagation issue.
kate: I updated customers: temporary fix applied, MS is working on control plane rollback, we're monitoring. Cust-alpha replied thanks, wants a postmortem.
azure-support: Support update: engineer suspects a rollback race during maintenance; their internal RCA will include fix and measures to prevent silent route deletions. They expect a code fix in 48-72h and a follow-up patch.
avery: We're going to keep incident open. Next: 1) run graceful failback after MS patch 2) run canary traffic to verify, 3) schedule postmortem and customer-facing summary.
lena: Assigning action owners: chen to keep working with MS + collect route diffs, john to validate app-level recovery and collect timeline, kate to coordinate customer comms.
ops-oncall: Handoff note: my shift ends in 35m, @avery please accept responder escalate if anything spikes.
avery: Accepted. If we see route withdraw again, plan B is spinning up sidecar NAT in eastasia and rerouting via private peering — more intrusive.
chen: Logging full route-table diffs and uploading to the incident artifact store: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-20270315-SEA-VWAN-ROUTE/route-diffs.log
john: Adding timeline snippet for PM: 02:12Z BGP withdraws -> 02:15Z alerts & paging -> 02:22Z Azure case opened -> 02:38Z manual static routes applied -> 02:45Z customer recovery.
kate: Customer impact summary for now: three customers experienced outage window ~02:12Z-02:45Z; severity: degraded for ~33 minutes. Postmortem and SLA credits TBD after investigation.
lena: Good. We'll keep this incident open until MS confirms patch and we complete cleanup. Prepare a short customer note for tomorrow.
incident-bot: Incident INC-20270315-SEA-VWAN-ROUTE updated: state -> monitoring. Next update in 30 minutes or on significant change.
(End of thread)
